title: US 224 over Eight Mile Creek | retained bridge with proposed 2026 repairs
source_note: Primary INDOT B-44532 / Des2200957 proposed 2026 repair set, document 9683628. Retained CB21 section and supports are checked against unchanged supplementary 1985/1986 B-16317 plans, document 9548292. Revision9707311 changes closure time only.
assumptions: Exterior visualization reconstruction of the named design state, not an as-built survey, structural rating or validated finite-element mesh.
No internal reinforcement, prestressing strands, embedded anchors or fabrication holes. Colors identify visualization layers; amber parts identify explicit approximations.
Source PDF page references always address drawings.pdf, an unchanged issued PDF. Supplemental historical pages are separately identified by document ID and local file.
Constructed interfaces and bearing contact checks establish geometric attachment only. Surveyed seats, actual camber, shim thicknesses and installed tolerances remain unknown.
Site terrain, channel solids, riprap individual stones, buried pile tips, full roadside guardrail terminals and nonstructural utility routing are omitted.
Latest primary coping width controls the 5 in discrepancy with historical revised slab width.
Native Z uses an illustrative 817 ft flowline datum; source grade and nominal beam contacts are reconstructed, not surveyed.
Void geometry is included to prevent a solid rectangular visual section from being mistaken for a hollow box. FEM section properties still require independent explicit calculation.

Actual deterioration and patch boundaries, wrap properties, bearing standard PB11 dimensions, slab/beam camber, wing footings and the retained lower wing walls, guardrail terminals, full drainage and site geometry.

known_deviations.source: sheet 9 (Overlay at Deck Drain Details, Section D-D, typical sections); sheet 8 note 7
known_deviations.deviation: The overlay keeps its full surface up to the 2 in drain cores; sheet 9 tapers the surface toward each mid-span drain over 1 ft 0 in (a 1 ft x 2 ft area along the face of rail).
known_deviations.reason: The taper area is dimensioned but its depth is not. "Taper Surface to Ex. Drain Edge" points to the existing drain edge, whose elevation is not given: it can be the milled slab (2 in below the finished surface, overlay feathered out), the unmilled deck ("Ex. Profile Grade + 1 1/2 in", 1 1/2 in below) or the drafted taper (about 1 in at 1 in = 1 ft in Section D-D). The Special Provision for Deck Drain Clean and Fill (sheet 8 note 7, not in the set) or a survey of the existing drain edges would settle it.

known_deviations.source: 1985 sheet 9 Detail A and Section B-B (Type 7B); Standard PB11 (not in the set)
known_deviations.deviation: Each beam end has one 0.23 m x 1.05 m x 50 mm pad envelope (generator assumption), parallel to the bearing line. 1985 sheet 5 calls for 12 Type 7B pads per abutment and Detail A (1985 sheet 9) draws them in pairs, one under each edge of the beam end.
known_deviations.reason: The pad length, width and thickness are on Standard PB11 (referenced on 1985 sheet 5), which is not in the set, and Detail A gives no pad dimensions or offsets (its 1/2 in = 1 ft scan is not reliable to scale for a pad), so the pairs cannot be placed without inventing their size; PB11 would settle it.

known_deviations.source: sheet 12 Section B-B and NE railing elevation; sheet 13; sheet 10 removal plan; 1985 sheet 6
known_deviations.deviation: At the NE corner the square TFC and RCBA extension start at the floor end on the 22 ft 0 in line (sheet 13), so between the skewed mudwall back face and that square end (up to 0.23 m along the railing back face) the new 7 ft 10 5/8 in railing has nothing under its back half. Sheet 12 Section B-B shows the existing wingwall there, and sheet 10 traces Wing C back to the floor end, but the 1985 plan (which the model follows for Wing C) starts the wing at the coping line. Rev. 1.4: the square end of the RCBA extension also passes 53 mm over the back corner of pavement_ledge_2 (a 0.03 m2 triangle in plan); the main slab beside it is thickened onto the ledge (sheet 15), the 1 ft extension is not.
known_deviations.reason: The outline of the existing wingwall root behind the mudwall at the NE corner is not dimensioned on either set; a field survey of the NE corner (or the pre-1985 plans) would settle it. Whether the extension end is thickened onto the ledge like the RCBA is on Standard Drawing E 609-TBAE (sheet 15 note 4), which is not in the set either.

known_deviations.deviation: Each slab root keeps the generator's 25 mm open joint along Line "A" (21.7 mm normal) to the mudwall back face and bears on the ledge from there; sheet 15 draws the RCBA end against the mudwall with a 1/2 in x 4 in preformed expansion joint filler at its foot, the Type I-A joint at the top and a 1/2 in x 2 in preformed filler on the back edge of the ledge, none of them modelled.

E 609-RCBA would settle the joint; the slab lengths and the RCBA extensions measured from the root are unaffected either way.
